 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Kishan Lal Vishnoi

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Urja Ram Kalbi, PP  Mr. Vijay Raj Bishnoi for complainant  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 10/01/2025 This application for bail under Section 483 BNSS has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.125/2024 registered at Police Station Gudamalani, Dist. Barmer, for the offences under Sections 450, 323, 341, 384, 366A, 354C,
376(2)(n), 376(3) of IPC and Sections 5(l)/6 of POCSO Act.
Heard learned counsel for the parties at Bar.
Perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that owing to prior revenue/ civil disputes between the parties, the petitioner has been roped in a false criminal case.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that initially, in the FIR, the complainant stated that victim 'M' was subjected to forcible sexual assault/rape by the petitioner about eight months prior to the date of lodging of [2025:RJ-JD:1845] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-14832/2024] the FIR.
The petitioner had also captured obscene videos and photographs of the victim 'M'.
In the FIR, it was further alleged that in the midnight of 19.06.2024, the petitioner entered in the the house of the complainant and held the victim 'M''s hand with bad intentions.
When she shouted for help, his wife came at the place of occurrence and rescued her.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that though the victim 'M' later on in her statements recorded under Section 183 of BNSS has alleged that she was subjected to forcible sexual assault/rape by the petitioner on 19.06.2024 but her mother- Mamta @ Saroj and one Lalita D/o Ashok Kumar in their statements recorded under Section 180 BNS have stated that on 19.06.2024, the petitioner touched the victim 'M' with wrong intentions and when she shouted for help, he ran away from the place of incident.

Learned counsel further contended that the FIR and the statements of Smt. Mamta @ Saroj and Lalita clearly indicates that the victim 'M' has given an exaggerated version of the alleged incident in her statements recorded under Section 183 BNSS.

Learned counsel submitted that no plausible explanation for lodging the FIR after a delay of more than eight months from the date when the victim 'M' was allegedly subjected to forcible sexual assault/rape by the petitioner for the first time, has been furnished by the prosecution.
Learned counsel submitted that no obscene videos and photographs allegedly captured by the petitioner to blackmail/ threaten the victim 'M' have been recovered by the investigating agency.

[2025:RJ-JD:1845] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-14832/2024] Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody; challan has already been filed and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused-petitioner.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that no plausible explanation for delay in lodging the FIR from the date when the victim 'M'
was subjected to forcible sexual assault/rape by the petitioner for the first time has been furnished by the prosecution.
The record of the case prima facie indicates that number of civil/revenue disputes are pending between the parties.

This Court having perused the FIR and the statements of Smt. Mamta @ Saroj and Lalita recorded under Section 183 (6)(a) BNSS is of the opinion that the possibility of victim 'M' giving an exaggerated version of the alleged incident which occurred on 19.06.2024 cannot be ruled out at this stage.

This Court also prima facie finds that the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the remaining material prosecution witnesses or fleeing away from justice or tampering with the evidence, in case he is enlarged on bail.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 BNSS is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Jay Ram @ Nuka Ram S/o Shri Pata Ram arrested in connection with F.I.R.
[2025:RJ-JD:1845] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-14832/2024

registered at Police Station Gudamalani, Dist. Barmer, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and Jay Ram @ Nuka Ram vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:1845) on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185934921/
